Florida is considering redirecting $200 million in federal electric vehicle charging funds toward air taxi infrastructure, a policy shift that could significantly accelerate the adoption of electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft. This potential reallocation aligns with recent industry momentum, including Joby Aviation’s progress toward Federal Aviation Administration certification and its recent $250 million funding round. The move signals a strategic pivot by state governments to prioritize aerial mobility over ground-based charging networks, potentially reshaping the competitive landscape for urban air mobility operators seeking public infrastructure support. [Florida is considering redirecting funds](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxOZGdndGJ3VE53eXNZWUxmcTY4T2UtM0pLMzY3UENFaDNTT0lGMHRwdk1OdFZTMmJHbUFOZkNIVnJFMjRjZk5DVC1zT19IMkFmb01GR3ptVGdkUy1veVY0VmdvZTN3ck9qeVkxeDZLZFBLVWR3QzNub3BoeVdiNGZUVXRrWDZZQWR2?oc=5)

In the autonomous vehicle sector, Kodiak AI is targeting a year-end launch of driverless trucking services on the Dallas-Houston corridor in partnership with IKEA. This development highlights the expanding commercial viability of autonomous freight operations, as companies seek to integrate self-driving technology into major retail supply chains. The initiative coincides with broader industry trends, such as Tesla’s Full Self-Driving becoming a sales driver for commercial fleets and WeRide’s potential expansion following a Slovakia alliance. These moves suggest a growing confidence in the reliability and economic efficiency of autonomous trucking for long-haul logistics. [Kodiak AI is advancing its autonomous trucking operations](https://news.google.?oc=5)

Counter-unmanned aircraft systems demand is rising as U.S. firm Powerus secured a $22.3 million contract to protect Middle East energy infrastructure from drone threats. This contract underscores the critical need for robust defense solutions in critical sectors, following AeroVironment’s strong financial performance after securing a $500 million Army contract. Simultaneously, the Federal Aviation Administration awarded $12 million for 19 drone research projects focused beyond visual line of sight operations, detect-and-avoid systems, and traffic management. These concurrent developments indicate a dual focus on both offensive drone capabilities and defensive countermeasures, as well as regulatory frameworks to safely integrate unmanned aircraft into national airspace. [Powerus has secured a $22.3 million contract](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiygFBVV95cUxOdkEwbjNiZFB0T3dHOWluU2NNa001NzNUZ3lGS3NNbmFLWHdwejRUY2ZZdWJJU3pmVWlHd0VOUnd4NGZNOExha2RGUkJ6NzZtTlhzR1pUd1FQb0lCV2tIMlFMUkY4cnRHQmJmUXhWUHZ4YWNpRUVrQlZUcW9wNWYwYUJSdHpCMFRJeFFGMjBXY0ZPYmxfZ0R4c0FWWndtWVpoR3BlYnhCMndzNFBfQnBBcEVBRmw3M1JPLWJXNFlCTERPeU1MRlBFem1B?oc=5)

Commercial drone delivery services are expanding rapidly, with Walmart and Wing announcing plans to expand drone deliveries to Denver and Seattle, offering delivery of thousands of items in as fast as 30 minutes. This expansion joins other major retailers entering the market, such as DoorDash, which stated its delivery drone is lighter and quieter than competitors. However, regulatory and legal challenges persist, as 15 U.S. states challenged the FAA’s environmental review of commercial drone package rules. Additionally, Amazon paused its North Haven drone plan due to public feedback, illustrating the complex interplay between technological advancement, consumer demand, and local regulatory acceptance. [Walmart and Wing will expand drone deliveries](https://www.9news.com/article/money/business/walmart-delivery-drones-denver-seattle/73-05416c06-4973-43f5-a9c9-74e477783599)
